speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long this painful ulcer on your leg has been present, and do you have any history of diabetes or vascular disease?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. Does the ulcer have raised, violaceous borders with a central area of healing, and have you noticed any joint pain or other skin lesions elsewhere on your body?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the purplish irregular borders and central necrosis, this presentation is highly suspicious for pyoderma gangrenosum, especially with your history of Crohn's disease. To help differentiate this from a vascular or infectious cause, can you tell me if you have experienced any recent changes in your bowel habits or abdominal pain?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: ["Crohn's disease", 'Type 2 diabetes mellitus', 'Hypertension', 'Treated for anterior uveitis 8 months ago'] Social history: Recently returned from a visit to Wisconsin 2 months ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: The travel history to Wisconsin raises the possibility of Sporotrichosis or other fungal infections, but the lesion's morphology and your Crohn's history strongly point toward Pyoderma Gangrenosum. I would like to confirm if the ulcer worsened after any attempt at surgical debridement or cleaning, a phenomenon known as pathergy. REQUEST TEST: Skin_Biopsy
